extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, mathematics education researchers, program evaluators, higher-education administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of the Mathematics and Education Reform (MER) Forum focused on measuring MER's influence on members' involvement in mathematics-education reform (postsecondary and K-12), the types and levels of support it provided, and the scope of its impact using surveys, site visits, observations, and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence on members' involvement in reform (postsecondary and K-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the extent to which MER influenced its members' involvement in mathematics-education reform at both postsecondary and K-12 levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure changes in participation, activities, and engagement attributable to MER across both undergraduate/postsecondary and K-12 contexts; consider both quantitative (e.g., participation rates) and qualitative evidence (e.g., self-reports, examples of activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for improving individual teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether MER provided support to mathematicians interested in improving their own teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of resources, workshops, peer support, changes in instructional practices, and reported impacts on individual teaching. Note that respondents often attribute only indirect effects to MER for changes in their teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership to mathematics departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether MER provided leadership to mathematics departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate department-level initiatives, leadership roles taken by MER participants, changes in departmental policies or priorities traceable to MER involvement, and examples from site visits and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimization of educational interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether MER legitimized members' educational interests within the academic mathematics community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess shifts in perceived legitimacy or acceptance of education-focused work among colleagues and departments, citations or references to MER as justification, and qualitative reports of increased credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of participation in undergraduate mathematics reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which MER facilitated faculty participation in the reform of undergraduate mathematics education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances of curricular changes, adoption of reform practices, collaborative projects, and participation rates in MER activities focused on undergraduate reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of participation in K-12 mathematics reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which MER facilitated faculty participation in K-12 mathematics education reform (noted in the report as to a lesser extent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect evidence of partnerships with K-12 schools, K-12 outreach activities, influence on K-12 curricula or teacher preparation, and barriers limiting MER's impact in this area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of changes to MER (direct vs indirect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mathematicians can attribute changes in their teaching or behavior directly to MER, or only indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between explicit causal attributions (participants saying MER caused a change) and indirect/partial attributions (MER influenced thinking or provided legitimization that contributed to change). Use survey self-reports and interview narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level/scope of impact (individual vs departmental vs broader)
rubrics_metrics.description: The level at which MER produced change — primarily individual-level impacts, with some departmental or broader institutional effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and classify observed impacts by scale: individual (personal teaching practice), departmental (departmental policies, curricula), and broader institutional or systemic change. Note predominance of individual-level effects as reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mixed-methods evaluation (survey, site visits, observation, interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation methodology used: survey of the entire national population of MER participants (n=730) with a 32% response rate; site visits to four university departments; participant observation at MER functions; and interviews with department personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat methodological breadth as a quality criterion: surveys for breadth, site visits and interviews for depth, and observations for contextual understanding. Record response rates and sample sizes to assess generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and instruments (workshop-evaluation questionnaire and survey instruments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and availability of evaluation instruments such as a workshop-evaluation questionnaire and copies of survey instruments (provided as appendices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate transparency and reproducibility by checking whether instruments, questionnaires, and protocols are included; these support assessment of validity and allow replication or adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program portrayal and dissemination guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for best portraying MER's program (recommended ways to present program aims, outcomes, and activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specifics are in the report, treat recommended portrayal strategies as part of program-improvement criteria — how the program is communicated to stakeholders, funders, and potential members to maximize perceived legitimacy and impact.
